neighbours.label: the restrictive clause that sets the limit of a recommendation in advice text ('only take what you need', 'a pace that you can keep'); the same relative clauses in narrative description stay quiet
fire: On a long flight, only bring what you can easily lift into the overhead bin.
When you start running, keep to a pace that you can hold for the whole route.
At the buffet, take only what you will actually eat.
For the exam, pick essay questions that you can answer with real examples.
Swim only in water that is shallow enough for you to stand up.
Before a move, keep just the furniture that you truly need in the new flat.
In a group chat, never write anything that you would be embarrassed to see forwarded.
On icy roads, steer at a speed that is slow enough to stop safely.
quiet: On a long flight last year, he lost the bag that held his passport.
When I started running, I met a neighbor who lived on the same street.
At the buffet, she found the dessert that her brother had made.
For the exam, the teacher printed questions that came from last year.
We swam in water that was warm and green from the algae.
Before the move, they sold the furniture that had belonged to their aunt.
In the group chat, someone posted a photo that showed the old school.
On the icy road, we passed a truck that had slid into a ditch.
